author: AlexanderWolf
quote:
Red Dead Redemption 3 in modern times. The sluggish controls on foot were okay in the Wild West, but they don't seem fitting in the modern game. Especially when driving is much more fast-paced, it creates a disconnect. 
The visuals are good on my ps5 pro, but not that much better than other games, overall, and the depth of field is driving me up the walls... with no ability to disable it. 
Story, until now, seems very bland, and it removed a lot of things that made the old GTA games so popular: causing chaos. Now the game does far too much to dissuade you from doing it, and even if you attempt to, it just doesn't work as well as it used to. 
Lucia's impulsive behavior is highly dislikeable, even more so than Amanda (Michael's wife in gta5). 
For the price they asked and the time it took, I'm rather disappointed.

author: AlexanderWolf
quote:
Loving every minute in it. It's basically a high fantasy mix of RedDead2 + Witcher 3 (+ maybe a drop of Dragon's Dogma 2). The controls are a bit clunky, due to just how many things you can do in-game, but I got used it to it quite fast.
Gameplay feels good overall, the world is awesome and always hidden things (and mechanics), and the story isn't as bad as the internet tried to make it (it ain't wow, but it's not bad either).

Based on how the game feels, and how much I've been able to find, randomly, in the 15h I had until now, I'm sure I'll enjoy this for at the very least 100h, potentially more. I've barely scratched the surface and it has more stuff to do and more replayability than many open world games have until their end. 
Money well spent.


By the way, ignoring my main pc's specs:It also runs 1200p Ultra settings, Native resolution (no upscale, no framegen), at 50-60fps on an Amd AI Max 395 handheld :)
So yeah, not bad at all in terms of performance. Path tracing is the only thing that makes the frames drop a lot. Otherwise, very well optimized.

author: AlexanderWolf
quote:
Generally speaking, I'm not a huge RE fan. I played some of the previous ones, but I couldn't really consider myself a fan of the series, to be honest. But I like to game, so I give many games a chance. Sadly, most of the time, that ends up in disappointment, BUT this time, it was very much the opposite.  I've had to struggle to find any complaints about it, and the only thing that I could come up with is that Grace was, at times in the campaign, far too emotionally illogical in her decisions, but I guess that can be realistic as well, if I think about it... 

Requiem managed to massively surprise me; from the atmosphere (yes, I know, I know, this is always the highlight of RE games) to the gameplay and the story, everything felt on point.  The gameplay differences in between characters was also quite refreshing (and awesome), although it created this duality situation, where in one circumstance it feels more of a scary/thriller, while in the the other, you're basically an action hero.  

I haven't been "hooked" by a game this way, to spend every available minute in it, for quite some time now.
By all intents and purposes, it won me over as a fan.

author: AlexanderWolf
quote:
Performance is abysmal even on my 14900KF+rtx5090. Crashes are often, mainly seeming to be connected to the lighting setting (switching to low or medium makes it that I get a crash per hour instead of one every 5 minutes, but I did not buy the most powerful gpu on the market to play on low settings because the devs are inept). Story and characters are impressively bland and forgetable, got myself more than halfway through the story, and I still don't feel any attachment to anyone in the game. The chars also feel very sanitized. No more tongue-in-cheek stuff, no more bad behavior. All are mr goody two-shoes, like in Veilguard.
Intentionally allowed a known npc to die in a main mission, although I could've easily saved him. Didn't matter, every other npc comforted me, telling me it wasnt my fault (yeah it was. Saving him was easy. Just chose not to, to see what happens). 

Yet another big AAA game that promises a lot and delivers very little. And what is delivered is unoptimized beyond any other game that I've played recently, while I have difficulties telling the visuals apart between this Borderlands4 and any of it's last 3 predecessors (BD2, BD3, Tiny Tina Wonderland). 

Even giving it a 2/10 feels overly generous.

author: AlexanderWolf
quote:
A proper successor to STALKER . The game gavea great feeling of nostalgia while improving on visuals and gameplay.
The story, at least until where I'm at now, feels compelling and practically keeps me glued to the screen, and the visuals are great and create an awesome atmosphere.
Of course it has some jank, it wouldnt be a STALKER game if it didnt, but in all honesty, the reason I gave it a 9 instead of a 10 is due to the voice acting: playing it in english, the characters sadly do not have the expected accent for that area.

Overall, a great game. Could've played it for free from my GamePass, but I chose to purchase it on Steam just to help them out a bit more. I consider the devs deserve it, for the game they've released.

author: AlexanderWolf
quote:
Copied from my Steam review: 

Dragon Age USED TO be a dark fantasy rpg involving an intricate story which your choices would change near and far term outcomes, with a complex system of companion **** then came **** dark fantasy part is gone, all replaced b y cheap one-line jokes and positivity. Conversations can only be of a positive note, no options at all to just be evil/mean/whatnot. Forced positivity and forced modern day, real life "problems" shoved into the game, and much of that is done through breaking the original lore. Even the visuals are "softened", both in terms of adding too much softening to textures (especially to skin), but also in terms of what you can create; simply look at how a Qunari looked in DA: Origins, DA2, DA:I, and compare the demonic horns and face with the... whatever that is now. Most characters just look goofy, but my main irk is indeed with the Qunari, since I finished DA:I multiple times playing as one simply because of the added difficulty (a fan will understand what that meant. The creators of Veilguard, on the other hand, **** element is practically gone. Few items that you upgrade over and over, few options to choose from in terms of what and how you can do. Dumbed-down spellcasing as well, because of course. The whole gameplay mechanic feels inspired by console action-rpg but the result came from temu , with the character running around from A to B , killing things by mashing the left click and rarely blocking/dodging a **** the point where I am in the game, I'm supposedly trying to stop two GODS from destroying and enslaving everyone. Should be some urgency to that, right? Nah, my companions busy making one-liner jokes and doing push-ups because they dared to misgender someone. The feel of urgency, of importance of your quest... it ain't there. The choices you have in conversations are all positive, and none of them change anything. There's no difference whether you try to use the kind reply or the "toughness" one, you'll still blurt out something positive, and everything will go on the same merry-go-lucky way, while supposedly attempting to stop a medieval magical FANTASY apocalypse.Actively feels like the developers of Veilguard had nothing to do with the previous DA games, and never bothered to look through the lore even a little bit, to get a glimpse of everything. Kind of reminds me of how Mass Effect Andromeda, which had a similar issue, making me think that maybe I should just stop spending money on Bioware and EA.I don't want and I don't need modern day problems and politics in a videogame. I need the videogame that I PAY for to follow the story and the universe it is in. And in this one, it feels like they were far, far too busy adding politics and trying to not offend anyone that they basically killed anything and everything that made Dragon Age a cult classic. Another great series ruined, in my eyes.I don't care about who cries about what on twitter. That modern audience talks a lot, cries a lot, but at the end of the day, it's me and others like me who have hundreds/thousands of games in their accounts. We're the ones paying, the old fans, filling the developer's bank accounts, and we're the ones playing. Keep doing this and we'll all stop. I, for one, will not buy ME5 or any other Bioware game from this moment onward.

author: AlexanderWolf
quote:
I was rather hyped about the idea of an "oldschool" AC game, but sadly this dlc sold as a game was not what I hoped it would be. The story itself is subpar, boring and easily forgettable. Quite a shame, given how the setting would have permitted for so much creativity...

- Gameplay/controls are probably the worst since Unity days. Many a times have I attempted to jump upwards on a ledge, only for Basim to decide "nah, I'm going to jump to the left and loose half my hp, instead". Feels overall clunky in terms of jumping, grabbing, etc. Even the animations are so much more limited compared to previous games. For example, the running assassination is always the same ONE animation. Even Unity had multiple ones, just to make it less boring. But not Mirage. 

- And then we get to the graphics part... To the average Joe, perhaps the game looks great. I will admit that looking from a distance, at the city, it looks amazing. But then if one decides to take a closer look, many of the textures and meshes are absolutely atrocious, closer in quality to games from 10 years ago. I stumbled in the beginning of the game to something that I believe it was supposed to be cut bamboo, but each "piece" of it was basically an octagon of low poly.

- In terms of characters, the vast majority, if not all, are easily forgettable; have yet to consider any in the game as being "memorable"  by any means, and the design of their faces, especially the random npcs looks absolutely horrible. 

- The fact that the game only required 40gb was supposed to have raised a red flag for me, but sadly, I was caught up in the hype. The low price of it was another red flag, given how Ubisoft games have generally costed 60-70euros, and this one, purchased through Ubisoft Connect app, was a bit under 50euros, should have raised a gigantic red flag. Somehow I didn't see it before playing it, but this game does NOT deserve any praise whatsoever, in my honest opinion. 

- Ah, yes, forgot to mention: main story+all sidequests done, missed only a few collectibles. Total playthrough, 19hours. IF you haven't bought it yet, don't. Wait until it's 10euros/dollars or less. That's the max I'd see this game being worth, and even so, I'm being generous.
